text:
ops-bot: ALERT: GPU queue length for prod-inference has grown > 1200. Autoscaler reports scale ceiling reached (maxNodes=50). Throttling incoming requests. Incident severity: high. Pager: @sre-oncall :rotating_light:

sre-oncall: acked. jumping in. first pass: is this isolated to prod-inference pool?

marta: yes, looks like eu-west-prod nodepool is saturated. pods pending due to node count limit. backlog started ~10:12 UTC.

devon: i'm seeing ~45k tokens/min waiting and many 429s from request router. customer impact: some low-latency customers reporting failures, queue timeouts increasing.

sre-oncall: thanks. can we get current node count and autoscaler config?

marta: current nodes=50 (max), desired=74 but capped. autoscaler config: maxNodes: 50, autoscale-policy: conservative-burst.

devon: logs from autoscaler:
```
I0615 10:21:33 autoscaler.go:201] Desired=74 Current=50 Max=50 -> ceiling reached
I0615 10:21:34 scaler_eval.go:88] scale decision blocked by maxNodes
```

infra-lead: oncall, can we do a temporary manual increase to 65 while we validate cost/approval? that's within our emergency allowances.

sre-oncall: request noted. who needs to approve?

devon: per policy, infra-lead or platform-eng eng-sig approval for up to +20 nodes in emergencies. infra-lead please approve.

infra-lead: approved. +15 nodes temporary. ops-bot: exec request: increase nodepool eu-west-prod maxNodes->65 and trigger scale.

ops-bot: Received manual override. Starting scale action. Running command: 
```
gcloud container node-pools update eu-west-prod --cluster=redwood-prod --max-nodes=65 --zone=eu-west1-b
kubectl apply -f autoscaler-emergency-patch.yaml
```

marta: running the update now, kube events show new nodes provisioning. ETA ~6-8 mins.

sre-oncall: monitoring queue and router. if we don't see drain in 10m escalate to infra pager.

devon: customer impact update: critical customers now degraded but not fully failed. we've toggled router fallback rules to route high-priority traffic to dedicated hosts to reduce visible errors.

marta: nodes coming up: 10m: 8 nodes ready; 12m: 14 nodes ready. pods starting to schedule, kube-scheduler logs show pods bound to new nodes.

ops-bot: Metric update: queue length dropping from 1200 -> 420 over 14m. token processing rate increasing.

sre-oncall: good. continue to observe for 30m. prepare rollback plan to revert maxNodes to 50 after stabilization.

devon: running a quick health-check script against representative customers — p99 latency improving, error-rate down 70%.

infra-lead: once stable for 20m, confirm and we'll keep manual bump for 2 hours then revert. also file incident ticket for postmortem.

marta: noted. filing incident in Jira: INF-4521. tagging for capacity/auto-scale owners.

sre-oncall: plan: 1) keep manual maxNodes=65 for 2h; 2) monitor queue until <50; 3) revert to 50 and observe for re-queue. if reappear, schedule config change to raise default maxNodes and tuning.

devon: FYI I'm publishing a brief customer-facing status note to status.redwood.ai: "We experienced degraded inference throughput due to autoscaling hitting capacity limits. We've applied a temporary increase and are restoring performance. We'll follow up with root cause and mitigation."

ops-bot: Update: queue < 100, error-rate back to baseline. Manual nodes still up.

infra-lead: great work. once we revert, include an explicit canary to watch for regressions. i'll join postmortem.

sre-oncall: closing oncall for now. leaving watch for 2 hours. tagging for follow-up: @infra-lead @marta @devon. :white_check_mark:
